text:
alex: FYI CI started failing on the new attention-kernel branch. fatbin size jumped ~12MB when LTO was flipped on for release build.

buildkite: build #4523 — fatbin_size_check: FAILED (delta=+12.3MB, threshold=+5%) :rotating_light:

alex: here's the relevant tail from the job that measures artifacts:
```
$ ./tools/ci/fatbin_stats.sh build/artifacts/kernel_fatbin.a
TOTAL_FATBIN: 58.2MB
PREV_BASELINE: 45.9MB
DELTA: +12.3MB (26.8%)
--- artifacts by SM ---
sm_70: 18.1MB
sm_75: 17.9MB
sm_80: 22.2MB
```

maria: oof. did we accidentally include duplicate PTX or unstripped device symbols? can you paste `cuobjdump --list-fatbin` or `nm` output?

alex: ran a quick `cuobjdump --dump-fatbin build/artifacts/kernel_fatbin.a | head -n 40` — looks like a bunch of identical kernels emitted per-arch plus large .debug symbols from the host toolchain LTO step. snippet:
```
fatbin(0): symbol count: 10234
fatbin(1): symbol count: 10226
fatbin(2): symbol count: 10231
// many identical symbol names across entries -> bloat by duplication
```

ben: two likely causes: (1) LTO is merging host sections into fatbin objects (we've seen some toolchains put host debug into device objects), (2) we might be embedding PTX+SASS for each arch variant instead of only the fallback PTX.

ben: quick mitigation options:
- pass `-fno-lto` (or `-Xcompiler -fno-lto`) to the host compiler for .cu linking stage so the device archives don't pick up host LTO artifacts
- switch to separate fatbin per SM instead of monolithic multi-arch fatbin (reduces duplication if we conditionally publish the right one per runtime)
- strip device-local symbol tables where safe: `cuobjdump --dump-sass | sed ...` followed by `nvdisasm`/`ptxas` flags if available

sarah: agreed. also differences in CUDA toolkit patchlevels change PTX encoding size a lot. the CI matrix currently builds with toolkit 11.7 and 12.1 on different runners — that mismatch can produce different ptx versions included. we should normalize the toolkit image used for size baseline runs.

alex: proposed immediate changes for CI to get us unblocked:
1) add a fast check that runs on PRs: `tools/ci/fatbin_size_check.py` that compares against baseline and prints per-SM breakdown (fail only on >15% increase for now).
2) add a `buildkite` job that builds with `-fno-lto` for a release candidate and compare sizes to isolate LTO impact.
3) capture `cuobjdump --dump-fatbin` artifacts for debugging and upload to the buildkite job.

maria: can we also change the linker invocation to pass `-Xlinker --gc-sections` / `-Wl,--strip-all` for host parts? Not sure how that interacts with nvcc-generated device blobs though.

ben: `--gc-sections` helps host objects but device blobs inside fatbins are opaque; their symbols are generated by the device toolchain. Stripping at the archive level (ar/objcopy on the generated .a) is worth trying. We should be careful with `--strip-all` — it can remove symbols we depend on for introspection.

ci-bot: triggered: buildkite pipeline "kernel-size-investigation" started by alex. artifacts will be retained for 7 days.

alex: I added a prototype PR with the CI changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/789 — the PR runs the `-fno-lto` build and uploads `cuobjdump` outputs.

maria: nice. what about long-term? we should avoid shipping huge multi-arch fatbins to hosted customers. maybe runtime can fetch per-arch variants and keep the hosted image small. that ties back to kernel-selection RFC.

ben: long-term ideas:
- publish a canonical "device-only" artifact (SASS-only) per SM and let deploy-time router choose which to load
- keep PTX-only fallback separate and only include PTX for older SMs to reduce duplication
- add a kernel linker step that deduplicates identical SASS across arch entries (hash and dedupe) — could cut repeated blobs by 30% if kernels are identical across minor SM versions

sarah: all good. for the near-term, can someone add the CI size gating change and the toolchain-image pin for the nightly baseline job? I can update the Docker images for toolchain 12.1 standardization.

alex: i'll land the PR with `-fno-lto` job and size check. ben can prototype the dedupe tool. maria/sarah handle the image pin. once we have the artifacts we can decide whether to strip or split.

maria: FYI local repro steps I used:
```
# reproduce fatbin from branch
make -j8 BUILD_TYPE=Release CUDA_VERSION=12.1
./tools/ci/fatbin_stats.sh build/artifacts/kernel_fatbin.a
cuobjdump --dump-fatbin build/artifacts/kernel_fatbin.a > /tmp/fatbin_dump.txt
```

ben: will add a small diagnostic script to `tools/ci` that extracts per-arch SASS size and a dedupe score. putting a threshold on dedupe score might be a better signal than absolute size in some cases.

alex: thanks everyone. filing a short follow-up RFC note in the kernel-selection thread about artifact format and CI gating after we have data.

buildkite: build #4524 — artifacts uploaded (cuobjdump output attached).

alex: attaching the buildkite link in the PR. marking this thread resolved for now.

sarah: :thumbsup: let's reconvene after the artifacts are analyzed.
